run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:21:38Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is consistent with the service's own evidence: frontend-proxy server ('ingress') spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR at a low but persistent rate (0.011–0.044 spans/s, ≈25 error ingress spans out of ≈18,200 non-error ingress spans in the last 30 minutes), while its client ('router frontend egress') spans never error. frontend-proxy's access logs show the errors are HTTP 503 responses with response flag UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} toward the upstream cluster 'frontend' (GET /, /api/cart, /api/products/*, /api/data, /api/recommendations), returned within microseconds. Those 503s were already occurring well before the alert's start (log lines from 01:00:21 and metric samples non-zero from 00:56:38 vs alert start 01:21:38), so the alert reflects a pre-existing low-level condition rather than a new deviation. No fault injection was enabled (all 12 flagd flags off), the frontend pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and its endpoint is present, and the frontend service records no error spans, so the terminating side is visible only indirectly through the Envoy response flag. The exact alert rule, the server-side reason the frontend closes connections, and any pre-00:54 baseline are unknown, hence partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's server-side span_name 'ingress' (span_kind SPAN_KIND_SERVER) records STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0.011–0.044 spans/s across the sampled window (first non-zero sample 00:56:38Z, last samples 01:22:38–01:27:38Z), giving 0.0333 in the same range as the alert's reported current value; the client span 'router frontend egress' shows STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 0 at every sample.

Over the 30-minute increase ending 01:29:01Z, frontend-proxy ingress error spans increased by ≈25.3 versus ≈18,176 non-error ingress spans (≈0.14%), and egress error spans increased by 0 — i.e. the errored requests are answered by the proxy itself and have no matching errored upstream client span.

frontend-proxy container logs (pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-p6mgt) contain repeated access-log lines with status 503 and response flag 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' pointing at the upstream cluster 'frontend', e.g. 'GET /api/cart' at 01:00:21Z, 'GET /' and 'GET /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4' at 01:21:14–01:21:15Z, 'GET /api/data/?contextKeys=travel' at 01:23:17Z, 'POST /api/checkout'-era 503s at 01:23:50Z and 'GET /api/recommendations?productIds=HQTGWGPNH4' at 01:25:20Z; every matched 4xx/5xx line in 01:00:00–01:13:06Z and 01:20:21–01:25:22Z is one of these 503 UC lines, and all other logged responses are 200 (with some 308 redirects).

The 503/error condition predates the alert's start of 01:21:38Z: error-span rate was already non-zero from the 00:56:38Z sample onwards and 503 UC access-log lines are recorded from 01:00:21Z, with the same sporadic pattern (zeros interleaved with 0.01–0.04 spans/s) both before and after 01:21:38Z.

The upstream named in the failing requests is the frontend service, and frontend looks healthy on its own signals: pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh is Running/Ready, restartCount 0, lastState empty, container started 00:41:47Z, and Service 'frontend' has a populated endpoint 100.96.2.139:8080; the frontend service records 0 error spans over the whole window while ad, fraud-detection and recommendation show only 2.0/2.0/3.0 error spans respectively, all on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (or '/flagd…EventStream') spans.

No flagd fault-injection setting is switched on: every flag in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant 'off' (value 0 or false).

The otel-demo workload layer is otherwise intact: all 21 deployments report 1/1 available and all 21 pods are Running with 0 restarts except fraud-detection (restartCount 1, container last terminated OOMKilled exitCode 137 at 00:47:07Z); all otel-demo pods were (re)started 00:41:42–00:43:35Z, i.e. as one namespace-wide start before the alert.

The grouped events inside the window contain no otel-demo objects at all: groups were Deployment(data-recorders/ScalingReplicaSet), Job, PersistentVolume, PersistentVolumeClaim, Pod, ReplicaSet and StatefulSet events, all in namespace data-recorders.

The frontend pods did not restart or become unavailable during the alert window (restartCount 0, no lastState, endpoint present) and frontend's own spans record no errors, so a frontend crash/unavailability is not supported by the evidence as the cause of the 503s.

Error spans in ad, fraud-detection and recommendation are confined to flagd EventStream spans (2–3 spans per 30 minutes), a long-lived streaming operation, and are not accompanied by any frontend-proxy ingress/egress error of the same kind; they are not evidence of impact through the frontend-proxy request path.

Fault injection through the demo's feature flags is rejected as the trigger: every flag in otel-demo/flagd-config is off, so no injected failure (adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, loadGeneratorFloodhouse-style flood, etc.) was active at query time.

The fraud-detection pod's OOMKill (exitCode 137 at 00:47:07Z, restartCount 1) is rejected as the cause of this alert: it is a different service, it predates the first observed 503 at 01:00:21Z, its error spans are flagd EventStream spans, and the 503s are connection resets on the 'frontend' upstream cluster.

The 503s look like a pooled-connection reuse race: failures complete in microseconds (logged 1–849 µs upstream response durations, 95 bytes, 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}'), the frontend returned no span at all for these requests, and requests to many different paths fail sporadically (~20 503s in ~25 minutes out of ~7.5 req/s) — consistent with the frontend closing an idle keep-alive connection at the moment frontend-proxy reuses it, but the frontend's own logs and keep-alive/idle configuration could not be read to confirm it.

The alert's firing is at least partly a threshold artefact: the reported current value 0.0333 matches the observed ingress error-span rate, which has been non-zero with no step change since the earliest available sample (00:56:38Z), so a rule that fires on any error rate above 0 would fire on this pre-existing background level; the rule's expression and 'for' duration could not be read.

Read the RequestErrorRate rule definition from the Alertmanager/Prometheus that holds it (it is not loaded in this target's Prometheus), confirm its expression and 'for' duration, and compare the pre-alert and post-alert frontend-proxy error level over equal windows before treating 01:21:38Z as an onset.

Compare the frontend server's HTTP keep-alive/idle timeout with frontend-proxy's upstream connection-pool idle settings and, if a mismatch is confirmed, align them or disable upstream keep-alive reuse as a test; this is the most likely way to eliminate the 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not present in this target's Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no rules, so its expression, threshold, 'for' duration and metric source are unknown and its firing cannot be tied to a specific evaluation transition.

No baseline before 00:54:38Z exists for frontend-proxy trace metrics (source_start_at 00:54:38Z) and Jaeger traces only reach ~00:54:33Z, while the whole namespace started 00:41:42–00:43:35Z; whether the 503 rate is new or has existed since the demo started is unknown.

The frontend container (pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh) produced no readable log lines for 01:00:00–01:29:00Z, and the frontend-proxy container has no previous instance, so the server-side reason the frontend terminates the connection (keep-alive close, stream timeout, internal error, resource pressure) could not be verified.

No sampled trace shows the failing requests: the 5 traces / 83 spans inspected around 00:54Z are all HTTP 200, and traces_search with error=true and otel.status_code="ERROR" for frontend-proxy returned nothing; the error spans visible in metrics have no matching Jaeger sample, so the failed requests' span graph is unknown.
Events cover only data-recorders objects (no otel-demo events), so any rollout, probe or scheduling events for frontend/frontend-proxy during the window are unknown.
The change-history integration is not integrated, so any configuration change to frontend keep-alive settings, frontend-proxy upstream pool settings or the alert rule before/at 01:21:38Z is unknown.
Node-level and per-container CPU/memory pressure on the node hosting frontend was not examined; it remains an unchecked alternative explanation for connection resets.
next_steps: Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alert rule (expression, threshold, for-duration) from the Prometheus/Alertmanager that evaluates it and record the last state transition time.
Inspect frontend-proxy's Envoy upstream cluster configuration (idle timeout, max connection duration, keep-alive settings) and the frontend Node.js server keep-alive/idle timeouts.
Collect frontend container logs (or enable/file a source that captures them) for a window covering 01:20–01:30Z to see whether the server logs connection aborts or handler errors.
Check pod/node-level resource metrics for the frontend pod and its node over 01:00–01:29Z to rule out CPU/memory pressure as the reason for connection termination.
Re-query the same error-span rate for a period after 01:29:01Z once the window extends, to establish whether the level changed or remained at the pre-alert background.
